schema: narrative analysis, regenerated whenever new data lands. the deterministic engine finds the facts; this reads them.
headline: The public data layer is complete and the private layer is empty. Every site on record came from a listing source, no owner has been contacted, and the top four counties on the screen hold no position at all.
state_of_play: Seventeen sites are on record. Eight carry a usable acreage figure at or above 500 gross acres; five have no acreage captured at all because the CoStar export was pulled without a lot-size column.
Nothing has moved past identified. There are no letters out, no conversations open, and no options drafted, so the pipeline has no conversion data to read yet.
The county screen is built and scored on hard USDA data. That layer is now the most reliable asset in the project — it is measured rather than estimated.
The contact universe is mapped but untouched. Twenty-two organisations are loaded and every one shows not_contacted.

what_the_data_says.point: Position and opportunity are almost perfectly inverted
what_the_data_says.detail: Six of the eleven sites with acreage sit in Ringgold, Davis and Taylor — counties scoring 47, 37 and 38. The four highest-scoring counties on the screen (Kossuth 88, Cherokee 85, Wright 81, Sac 79) hold zero sites. The portfolio is concentrated in the bottom of the screen.

what_the_data_says.point: Assemblage difficulty is the cleanest discriminator in the dataset
what_the_data_says.detail: Owners per section ranges from 2.7 in Cherokee to 10.2 in Dallas. Two sites sit in Davis County at 7.4 and one in Dallas at 10.2 — meaning a full-section footprint there needs roughly three times the signatures it needs in the top counties, for worse ground.

what_the_data_says.point: Kossuth is the single largest untouched pool in the state
what_the_data_says.detail: 396 farms at 500+ acres and 143 above 1,000, at a median of 228 acres — 2.8 owners per section. No site, no contact, no activity. Two loaded contacts already cover it: NIACOG and Mid Iowa Growth Partnership.

what_the_data_says.point: One recorded fact is worth more than the rest and is unverified
what_the_data_says.detail: The Lohrville listing states no county zoning in Calhoun. If true it removes the rezoning path entirely on a 613-acre tract on flat ground. It is a phone call and it has not been made.

what_the_data_says.point: Three of the strongest sites are on auction timelines
what_the_data_says.detail: Albert City, Lohrville and Sanborn all came from auction listings. Auction ground moves on a fixed date rather than a negotiation, so these are the only records in the pipeline with an externally imposed clock.

watchlist: Taylor County drafted a moratorium ordinance on 8 June 2026 and one site sits inside it. Status unconfirmed since.
Sioux and Plymouth are closed, and both border O'Brien where a site is held. Ordinance contagion moves along county lines.
Five sites carry no acreage. Until that is filled they cannot be ranked and are effectively invisible to the screen.
No owner names are recorded anywhere in the dataset. Every site is known only through a broker or listing, which means no direct approach is possible yet.
if_nothing_else: Two calls close the largest gaps in the dataset at once: Mid Iowa Growth Partnership covers Kossuth, Wright, Calhoun and Hardin — four of the top counties and two pipeline sites — and IADG is already the listing contact on two sites while representing 250 utilities across the rural counties where the screen points.
